channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: bun install: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen
item.description: CI runs bun install --frozen-lockfile so a build can never silently resolve different versions. The error means package.json and bun.lock disagree — usually because a dependency was edited by hand without re-running install locally.

item.title: Cargo: lock file version requires a newer version of Cargo
item.description: Cargo.lock carries a format version. A newer toolchain wrote a version this Cargo cannot parse — typically a contributor or CI image on a newer Rust than the pinned one.

item.title: CORS: credentialed request cannot use a wildcard origin
item.description: When a request sends cookies or an Authorization header, the browser requires Access-Control-Allow-Origin to name one exact origin. A wildcard is rejected, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials must be true as well.

item.title: docker buildx: no builder instance found
item.description: buildx needs a builder backed by BuildKit. On a fresh install, in CI, or after docker context switching there may be no builder configured, so any buildx build or multi-platform build fails before it starts.

item.title: docker-compose: command not found
item.description: Compose V1, the standalone Python binary invoked as docker-compose, reached end of life and is no longer installed. Compose is now a Docker CLI plugin invoked as docker compose, with a space.

item.title: docker: manifest unknown
item.description: The registry has the repository but not the tag or digest you asked for. Common causes are a typo, a tag that was never pushed for your architecture, or an image whose tags were pruned by a retention policy.

item.title: ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached
item.description: A dev server or file watcher exhausted the per-user inotify watch limit. Despite the ENOSPC name there is no disk problem — each watched directory consumes one kernel watch and large node_modules trees run through the default allowance quickly.

item.title: ESLint: could not find an eslint.config.js file
item.description: ESLint v9 reads flat config (eslint.config.js) by default and no longer looks for .eslintrc.*. An existing project that only has .eslintrc.json therefore looks unconfigured to the new binary.

item.title: FastAPI: ResponseValidationError
item.description: The handler returned data that does not match its response_model. Unlike a request validation error this is a 500, because the fault is on the server: FastAPI will not serialise a response that breaks the documented schema.

item.title: GitHub Actions: OIDC token request failed — not authorized
item.description: The workflow tried to exchange a GitHub OIDC token for cloud credentials but was refused. Either the job did not request the id-token permission, or the trust policy's subject condition does not match this repository, branch or environment.

item.title: go: toolchain not available
item.description: Since Go 1.21 a go.mod may name a newer toolchain than the installed one. Go normally downloads it, but with GOTOOLCHAIN=local, no network, or a restricted proxy it cannot, and the build stops.

item.title: Helm: cannot patch — field is immutable
item.description: An upgrade changed a field Kubernetes does not allow to be updated in place, such as a Deployment's selector, a Job's template, or a PVC's storage size downward. Helm's patch is rejected by the API server.

item.title: JWT: token used before issued / not valid yet
item.description: Validation compared the token's iat or nbf claim against the verifier's clock and decided the token is from the future. The token is fine; the two machines' clocks disagree, often by seconds in a container without NTP.

item.title: Kubernetes: exceeded quota in namespace
item.description: A ResourceQuota caps what the namespace may request in aggregate. The create is rejected at admission time, so a Deployment can exist while its ReplicaSet never produces pods — the reason only appears in the ReplicaSet events.

item.title: Kubernetes: no matches for kind in version — removed API
item.description: The manifest uses an apiVersion the cluster no longer serves. Kubernetes removes beta APIs on a published schedule, so a chart or manifest that worked on an older cluster stops applying after an upgrade.

item.title: Kubernetes: violates PodSecurity restricted:latest
item.description: Pod Security Admission is enforcing the restricted profile on the namespace and the pod spec does not meet it — typically because it runs as root, allows privilege escalation, or does not drop all capabilities.

item.title: MySQL: Authentication plugin 'caching_sha2_password' cannot be loaded
item.description: MySQL 8 made caching_sha2_password the default authentication plugin. An older client library that only implements mysql_native_password cannot complete the handshake.

item.title: Next.js: Event handlers cannot be passed to Client Component props
item.description: A Server Component tried to pass a function (onClick, onChange) across the server/client boundary. Functions cannot be serialised into the RSC payload, so the render fails.

item.title: Node.js: error:0308010C:digital envelope routines::unsupported
item.description: Node 17+ links OpenSSL 3, which refuses the legacy MD4 hash that older Webpack 4 builds use for chunk names. The build breaks even though nothing in your code changed.

item.title: OpenTelemetry: connection refused exporting to the collector
item.description: The SDK could not reach an OTLP endpoint. Almost always the port or protocol is wrong: 4317 is OTLP/gRPC and 4318 is OTLP/HTTP, and the HTTP exporter needs the /v1/traces path unless the SDK appends it.

item.title: OpenTofu: state is encrypted but no key provider is configured
item.description: OpenTofu can encrypt state and plan files at rest. Once a state has been written encrypted, every later run needs the same key provider configured, or the state cannot be read back.

item.title: PgBouncer: prepared statement already exists
item.description: In transaction pooling mode a client can land on a different server connection each transaction. A driver that caches server-side prepared statements then re-prepares a name that already exists on that backend.

item.title: Playwright: strict mode violation — locator resolved to multiple elements
item.description: Playwright locators are strict by design: if a selector matches more than one element it refuses to act rather than silently picking the first. The message lists every element that matched.

item.title: Podman: short-name did not resolve to an alias
item.description: Unlike Docker, Podman does not assume Docker Hub for an unqualified image name. In non-interactive mode it refuses to guess which registry "nginx" means, because that choice is a security decision.

item.title: Poetry: pyproject.toml changed significantly since poetry.lock was generated
item.description: Poetry stores a hash of the dependency section in the lock file. Editing pyproject.toml by hand invalidates it, and Poetry refuses to install rather than guess which versions you meant.

item.title: PostgreSQL: canceling statement due to lock timeout
item.description: The statement waited longer than lock_timeout for a lock another transaction held. This is usually a migration queuing behind a long-running query, and the cancellation is protecting you from an unbounded stall.

item.title: pytest: async def functions are not natively supported
item.description: pytest collects an async test, has no event loop to run it in, and skips the body — so the test reports as passed or warns while asserting nothing. A plugin has to drive the coroutine.

item.title: Python 3.12: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'distutils'
item.description: distutils was deprecated in 3.10 and removed from the standard library in Python 3.12. Any package whose setup.py or runtime code imports it fails immediately on a 3.12+ interpreter.

item.title: React 19: useFormState is deprecated — use useActionState
item.description: React 19 moved the form-action state hook out of react-dom and renamed it. Code importing useFormState from react-dom warns, and in newer builds the import is simply missing.

item.title: systemd: start request repeated too quickly, refusing to start
item.description: The unit crashed and restarted more times than StartLimitBurst allows within StartLimitIntervalSec, so systemd stopped trying. The rate limit is a symptom — the real failure is whatever made the service exit, and it is in the journal.

item.title: Tailwind CSS v4: unknown at-rule @tailwind
item.description: Tailwind v4 replaced the three @tailwind directives with a single @import, and moved PostCSS support into a separate package. A v3 stylesheet or PostCSS config left in place stops producing any utilities.

item.title: Terraform: Cycle — resources depend on each other
item.description: Terraform builds a dependency graph from references and cannot order a cycle. Two resources referencing each other's attributes, or a badly placed depends_on, makes the plan impossible rather than merely slow.

item.title: Terraform: provider checksum list has no SHA-256 hash
item.description: The dependency lock file records provider hashes per platform. When it was generated on one OS and CI runs on another, the recorded hashes do not cover the platform being installed and Terraform refuses to proceed.

item.title: uv: No solution found when resolving dependencies
item.description: uv resolves the whole dependency graph at once and reports the exact conflicting constraints rather than installing something that half works. The message names the two requirements that cannot both be satisfied.

item.title: Vite: the CJS build of Vite's Node API is deprecated
item.description: Something loaded Vite through require() instead of an ES import — usually a vite.config.js in a package without "type": "module", or a plugin that still uses CommonJS. It is a warning in Vite 5 and an error once the CJS build is removed.

item.title: Vitest: No test suite found in file
item.description: Vitest loaded the file but it registered no test() or describe() calls. Usually the suite is inside a conditional, the file was matched by the include glob but is really a helper, or an import threw before the tests were registered.

item.title: Yarn PnP: a package tried to access an undeclared dependency
item.description: Plug'n'Play enforces the dependency graph strictly: a package may only require what it declares. Code that relied on a hoisted node_modules layout breaks because the transitive package is no longer reachable.

item.title: 402 Payment Required
item.description: Reserved in the original HTTP specification and now used by many SaaS APIs to signal that the account is unpaid, out of credit, or over its plan limit. The response body carries the vendor-specific detail.

item.title: 421 Misdirected Request
item.description: The server received a request for a host it cannot serve on that connection. With HTTP/2 connection coalescing, a browser may reuse one TLS connection for several hostnames covered by the same certificate; if the server is not configured for one of them it answers 421.

item.title: 428 Precondition Required
item.description: The server requires the request to be conditional. It is telling the client to send If-Match or If-Unmodified-Since so that concurrent updates cannot silently overwrite one another (the lost update problem).

item.title: 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
item.description: The combined size of the request headers exceeded the server's limit. In practice this is nearly always cookies: an accumulation of analytics, session and feature-flag cookies on one domain.

item.title: 511 Network Authentication Required
item.description: A captive portal — hotel, airport or corporate guest Wi-Fi — is intercepting traffic and requires sign-in. The response comes from the network, not from the server you addressed.

item.title: Android: Duplicate class found in modules
item.description: Two dependencies bring in the same class, usually because one ships a bundled copy of a library that another declares normally, or because two versions of the same artifact are on the classpath under different coordinates.

item.title: Anthropic API: invalid_request_error on tool_use / tool_result
item.description: Tool calling requires strict message pairing: every assistant tool_use block must be answered by a user message containing a tool_result with the matching tool_use_id, in the immediately following turn.

item.title: AWS Bedrock: AccessDeniedException — you don't have access to the model
item.description: Bedrock foundation models must be explicitly enabled per account and per region before they can be invoked, in addition to the usual IAM permissions.

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime exited with error: signal: killed
item.description: The function process was killed for exceeding its memory allocation. Lambda reports this rather than an application-level OOM, so the stack trace is absent.

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime.ImportModuleError
item.description: The runtime could not load the handler module. Either the handler string does not match the file and export, a dependency is missing from the package, or a native module was built for the wrong architecture or OS.

item.title: AWS S3: SignatureDoesNotMatch
item.description: The SigV4 signature computed by the client differs from the one S3 computed. Causes: wrong secret key, clock skew beyond five minutes, the wrong region in the signing scope, or a proxy that altered headers after signing.

item.title: AWS: AccessDenied when calling the AssumeRole operation
item.description: Role assumption requires permission on both sides: the caller needs sts:AssumeRole in its identity policy, and the target role's trust policy must name the caller as a principal. A denial on either side produces the same message.

item.title: AWS: ExpiredToken / The security token included in the request is expired
item.description: Temporary credentials from STS, IAM Identity Center (SSO) or an assumed role have passed their expiry. Sessions are short-lived by design — one hour by default for an assumed role.

item.title: Azure OpenAI: DeploymentNotFound
item.description: Azure OpenAI addresses a *deployment name* you chose, not the underlying model name. Passing 'gpt-4o' when the deployment is called 'prod-gpt4o' returns 404 DeploymentNotFound.

item.title: Azure: MissingSubscriptionRegistration — resource provider not registered
item.description: Azure requires each resource provider namespace to be registered on the subscription before resources of that type can be created. New subscriptions have only a small default set registered.

item.title: bash: Argument list too long
item.description: A glob expanded to more arguments than the kernel's exec limit allows. The limit is on the total size of arguments plus environment, so a large environment makes it hit sooner.

item.title: bash: bad interpreter: No such file or directory
item.description: The script's shebang line ends with a carriage return, so the kernel looks for an interpreter literally named "/bin/bash\r". The file was saved with Windows line endings, usually via a Git checkout with autocrlf enabled.

item.title: C#: CS8618 non-nullable property must contain a non-null value when exiting constructor
item.description: With nullable reference types enabled, the compiler requires every non-nullable member to be definitely assigned by the end of the constructor. It is warning that the object can be observed in an invalid state.

item.title: C++: runtime error: signed integer overflow (UBSan)
item.description: Signed integer overflow is undefined behaviour in C and C++. The program may appear to work for years and then miscompile after an optimiser change, so UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer reporting it is a real bug, not a false positive.

item.title: cert-manager: Order is pending / challenge failed to propagate
item.description: cert-manager created an ACME order but the challenge never validated. For HTTP-01 the challenge path is not reachable from the internet; for DNS-01 the TXT record has not propagated or the credentials lack permission.

item.title: Cloudflare 520: Web server returns an unknown error
item.description: Cloudflare reached the origin but received a response it could not parse — an empty reply, a connection reset mid-response, oversized headers, or a violation of the HTTP specification.

item.title: Cookie: SameSite=None requires the Secure attribute
item.description: Browsers reject a cookie that declares SameSite=None without Secure. Cross-site cookies must be sent over HTTPS only, so the pair is mandatory. The cookie is silently dropped, which usually shows up as a session that never persists.

item.title: CSP: Refused to execute inline script because it violates the policy
item.description: Content-Security-Policy blocked an inline or an inline event handler. This is the policy preventing the main injection vector for XSS, so the fix is to make the script legitimate rather than to weaken the policy.
